validity.recommendation: Check whether Owner1 should cover only the Ukrainian section; settle start year 1973 versus 1975.
validity.researcher_notes: The line is real. A 2015 Ukrtransgaz statement and Moldovatransgaz's own list both name Rozdilna-Izmail with 230 km, 820 mm and 7.3 bcm per year, matching the sheet. Caveats: the line crosses Moldova and Transnistria, so one Ukrainian owner at 100 percent overstates it. Start year is 1975 in one source and October 1973 in Ukrainian Wikipedia. Moldovatransgaz also lists the Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Izmail line with the same 820 mm and 7.3 bcm figures, so the two should not be merged without care. Row P0784 is the one that mixes them.

verifications.note: Ukrtransgaz statement from July 2015: Раздельная-Измаил, протяженность 230 км

fills.researcher_notes: A news report from July 2015 quotes Ukrtransgaz, the operator at the time, giving the length of the Rozdilna-Izmail line as 230 km. This matches the sheet. The Moldovan trunk-line list gives 92.24 km, but that is only the part on Moldovan soil. I did not search for a second source.

verifications.note: Раздельная - Измаил (РИ) ... 820 мм и пропускной способностью 7,3 млрд м3 в год

fills.researcher_notes: Two separate publishers give 7.3 bcm per year for this line. One is Ukrtransgaz, quoted in a July 2015 news report. The other is Moldovatransgaz, in its own list of trunk lines (web capture from October 2022). Both match the sheet.
Moldovatransgaz's list of trunk lines gives 820 mm for Rozdilna-Izmail. Ukrainian Wikipedia's article on the Shebelinka-Izmail corridor says the same. Both match the sheet.
The July 2015 Ukrtransgaz statement describes a natural gas trunk line.

Both sources name the line as Rozdilna to Izmail, both in Odesa Oblast. The line crosses Moldova, including a stretch in Transnistria, between the two Ukrainian end points. The Moldovan section is about 92 km according to Moldovatransgaz.

A Transnistrian news item from November 2015 says the trunk line was put into service in 1975. This matches the sheet. Ukrainian Wikipedia says deliveries on Rozdilna-Izmail began in October 1973, and the shebelinka corridor line (ШДКРІ) started in 1975. So the start year is contested between 1973 and 1975. I kept the sheet value and filed a note.

verifications.note: Ukrtransgaz 2019: Раздельная-Измаил named for reverse gas supply from Romania from January 2020
capital repair of the line planned, July 2015

fills.researcher_notes: A 2019 report names Rozdilna-Izmail as one of two lines meant to carry gas from Romania starting January 2020. A 2015 report describes planned capital repairs. Neither source is dated 2024 or later. I found no source saying the line is idle or shut.

fills.researcher_notes: I did not find a page naming this line and its owner today. Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine runs the national system, but its website blocks this machine and the web archive was offline. The 2015 statement names Ukrtransgaz, the earlier operator. Moldovatransgaz says it runs about 92 km of the line in Moldova, and a Transnistrian company runs about 34 km. So 100 percent ownership by the Ukrainian operator is doubtful for the whole line.
Searched for the current operator by line name. The only dated source names Ukrtransgaz in 2015, before the 2020 split. The operator's own site blocks this machine. Not filled.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: No source dated 2024 or later names this line. A December 2025 Amber Grid presentation shows gas flowing into Ukraine from Romania through the Orlivka-Isaccea point in 2025, so the southern system near Izmail is in use. That does not name Rozdilna-Izmail. Kept as operating. The evidence covers the Ukrainian section only.

summary: "Real line, specs match 2015 Ukrtransgaz and Moldovatransgaz; owner 100% doubtful (cross-border); start 1973 vs 1975; Owner/Operator unresolved"
